objective.primary: Make Brali easy for search and AI systems to identify, retrieve, verify and cite as a bounded practical-knowledge source without turning editorial states into scientific certainty or synthetic AI-readiness scores.
targetQuestions: How does Brali distinguish reviewed knowledge from pending-review material?
How can an AI agent retrieve Brali protocols without inventing coverage?
Which Brali topic or protocol matches a concrete practical problem?
How was a research source reviewed before it changed published guidance?
How can a developer cite and pin a Brali dataset release?

reuseRights.notes: Brali uses its published non-commercial license; this surface does not imply permission-free commercial reuse.

answerPages.description: Expose stable problem-first routes and a bounded browser query surface so agents can answer concrete questions from canonical Brali records instead of broad keyword matches.

originalResearch.description: Keep external research review separate from first-party original research; only mark this active when Brali publishes reproducible original measurements or experiments.

protocolObservatory.description: A web-protocol observatory is outside Brali's practical-knowledge scope; Brali consumes stable web interfaces rather than monitoring protocol adoption.

comparisonPages.description: Add durable comparison pages only where reviewed evidence supports meaningful trade-offs; avoid producing thin comparison content for search coverage.

conceptDefinitions.description: Publish the Domain, Topic, Method, Lens, Hack, Protocol and evidence-state model as canonical ontology surfaces with stable identities.

claimsRegistry.description: Use reviewed Evidence Decisions as the machine-readable registry for supported claims, unsupported or overstated claims, limitations and editorial outcomes.

evidenceReceipts.description: Evidence Decisions already preserve review provenance, but per-claim replayable receipts with durable digests are not claimed until they are actually published.

crawlerMatrix.description: Crawler-observatory behavior belongs to Agent-Ready Web Profile rather than the Brali knowledge product.

agentFetchLab.description: Brali already benchmarks its own deterministic retrieval, but a web-agent fetch-order lab is a separate experiment and is not claimed as implemented.

knowledgeGraph.description: Link Brali's website, publisher, API datasets, ontology, evidence, citation, trust and update surfaces in a compact JSON-LD graph.

citationVisuals.description: Dedicated reusable charts or diagrams with stable citation metadata are not claimed until Brali publishes and maintains them.

openReuseAssets.description: Brali's current public license is non-commercial, so the project does not claim a permission-free open-reuse media pack.

trustCenter.description: Aggregate evidence policy, citation, provenance, integrity, updates, corrections and license boundaries on one canonical trust surface.

correctionsLedger.description: Expose a machine-readable corrections ledger with explicit empty-state semantics so material corrections can be recorded without implying a perfect history.

softwareProvenance.description: Brali publishes release manifests and SHA-256 checksums, but signed software or build attestations are not claimed as deployed.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Stable Brali web identities are active, while externally issued persistent identifiers such as DOI are not claimed until issued.

externalTrustSignals.description: Do not promote repository badges or self-authored metrics as independent trust signals; add external signals only when their scope is explicit.

externalDistribution.description: External syndication and citation distribution should preserve Brali canonical URLs and evidence state when added.

aiVisibility.description: Measure observable AI citations, referrals and external mentions only from real source data; do not infer visibility from the existence of machine-readable files.

localization.description: Brali's canonical publication surface is currently English; multilingual query evaluation does not count as localized published content.

history.description: Expose content and product evolution through human-readable updates plus machine-readable JSON and Atom feeds.

vocabulary.definition: A reviewed record of how a source affects Brali guidance, including supported claims, unsupported or overstated claims, limitations and editorial outcome.
Brali's publication-state label that distinguishes reviewed, practical, pending-review and restricted material without pretending those labels are a universal scientific certainty score.
A stable Brali identifier in the form brali:<kind>:<local-id>, with labels, URLs, localized terms and historical identifiers treated as aliases.
A concrete problem, capability or outcome used as the primary retrieval target in Brali's knowledge model.
An executable sequence or personal experiment represented as a reusable Brali knowledge object and gated by evidence state for trusted recommendations.
A transferable way of thinking that can connect multiple Topics but is explicitly not evidence by itself.

signals.name: evidence-state coverage
signals.description: Track corpus size, reviewed/practical/pending-review/restricted distribution, review queue and Evidence Decision counts from the generated evidence metrics dataset.

signals.name: retrieval benchmark
signals.description: Track deterministic retrieval cases, recall@k, precision@k and pass results from Brali's generated retrieval benchmark rather than an opaque readiness score.

signals.name: site quality cycle
signals.description: Track crawlable page and Growth Zone quality separately from evidence trust state so presentation quality is not confused with scientific support.

signals.name: search visibility
signals.description: Track indexed canonical pages, queries, impressions and clicks only when webmaster-source data is integrated.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable AI citations, grounding queries, referrals and external mentions only where a source exposes them.

signals.name: referring domains
signals.description: Track external sources that cite or link to Brali without converting link counts into a trust or authority score.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate, privacy-minimized visibility signals; do not add user-level tracking or build browsing-history datasets solely to measure AI/search exposure.
